paper.title_en: Measuring Charged Current Muon Neutrino Cross Sections on Oxygen with the Accelerator Neutrino Neutron Interaction Experiment
paper.abstract_en: The Accelerator Neutrino Neutron Interaction Experiment (ANNIE) is a $26$-ton gadolinium-doped water Cherenkov detector on-axis of the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) at Fermilab. With ANNIE, this dissertation provides the first results of a high statistics muon neutrino charged current cross section on oxygen at a short baseline on axis. This thesis explains the necessity of the measurements and details how the measurements are performed. Focus is given on the physics behind the models used to predict neutrino cross sections. The measurements include the CC inclusive and CC$0\pi$ cross section channels. This thesis details the processes of event selection, reconstruction, handling systematics, and unfolding as part of cross section measurements. A data unblinding procedure is documented and acts as the first implementation of data unblinding in ANNIE. These results provide additional constraints on existing neutrino interaction models and are the necessary steps for a joint analysis with liquid Argon experiments also on the BNB line.
